doc.title: Art Farmer — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Bird's Camarillo breakdown and later meeting at Small's Paradise
summary: Bird's California recordings came after Farmer left; Bird was committed to Camarillo and greeted him later in New York.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Did you go to any of the sessions that Bird did out in California with Howard McGhee…

No, those sessions happened after I left. What happened was that when I was still there, Dizzy had left, Bird was still in town, and he did some recording, and something happened to him where he really flipped, and he wound up in a place called Camarillo. He did the sessions when he got out of Camarillo. By that time, I was back east with Johnny Otis’ band. Next time I saw Bird was here in New York, uptown at Small’s Paradise. He says, “Hey, Arthur Farmer! We’re in New York, man! You can get anything you want in New York.”
